questions.stem: Ms. Cho asked ___ to review the contract before the meeting.

fr.rule: Après un verbe (asked), on emploie le pronom complément.
why_wrong: A : adjectif possessif, il faudrait un nom derrière.
B : pronom sujet, mais ici il s'agit du complément.
C : pronom possessif : sens incorrect.

en.rule: After a verb (asked), use the object pronoun.
why_wrong: A: possessive adjective, a noun would be needed.
B: subject pronoun, but this is an object position.
C: possessive pronoun: wrong meaning.

questions.stem: The company announced ___ new office policy on Monday.

fr.rule: Avant un nom : adjectif possessif. Its (sans apostrophe) pour un sujet singulier non humain.
why_wrong: A : pronom possessif, sans nom derrière.
C : contraction de « it is », pas un possessif.
D : le sujet « company » est singulier.

en.rule: Before a noun: possessive adjective. Its (no apostrophe) for a singular non-human subject.
why_wrong: A: possessive pronoun, with no noun after it.
C: contraction of 'it is', not a possessive.
D: the subject 'company' is singular.

questions.stem: The new laptop on the desk is ___, not Tom's.

fr.rule: Pronom possessif quand aucun nom ne suit.
why_wrong: A : réfléchi : mauvais emploi.
B : adjectif possessif : un nom devrait suivre.
D : pronom complément.

en.rule: Possessive pronoun when no noun follows.
why_wrong: A: reflexive: wrong use.
B: possessive adjective: a noun should follow.
D: object pronoun.

questions.stem: The manager completed the audit by ___ in just two days.

why_wrong: B : pronom possessif.
C : pronom sujet.
D : pronom complément : pas de sens d'insistance.
B: possessive pronoun.
C: subject pronoun.
D: object pronoun: no emphasis meaning.

questions.stem: The two departments share information with ___.

fr.rule: Each other exprime la réciprocité entre deux sujets.
why_wrong: A : adjectif possessif.
C : ne marque pas la réciprocité.
D : un réfléchi ne convient pas à une action réciproque.

en.rule: Each other expresses reciprocity between two subjects.
why_wrong: A: possessive adjective.
C: does not mark reciprocity.
D: a reflexive does not fit a reciprocal action.

questions.stem: The manager asked the assistants to finish the work ___.

fr.rule: Pronom réfléchi pour insister ou renvoyer au sujet.
why_wrong: A : Pronom possessif, sens incorrect.
C : Adjectif possessif : il demande un nom.
D : Pronom objet simple ; ici on insiste sur « eux-mêmes ».

en.rule: Reflexive pronoun for emphasis or to refer back to the subject.
why_wrong: A: Possessive pronoun, wrong meaning.
C: Possessive adjective: needs a noun.
D: Simple object pronoun; here the emphasis is 'by themselves'.

questions.stem: This laptop is not mine; it must be ___.

fr.rule: Pronom possessif (mine, hers, theirs) = sans nom après.
why_wrong: B : Pronom réfléchi : sens incorrect.
C : Adjectif possessif : il faudrait un nom (« her laptop »).
D : Pronom sujet.

en.rule: Possessive pronoun (mine, hers, theirs) = no noun after.
why_wrong: B: Reflexive pronoun: wrong meaning.
C: Possessive adjective: needs a noun ('her laptop').
D: Subject pronoun.

questions.stem: The two companies have agreed to share information with ___.

fr.rule: Each other = réciprocité entre deux sujets.
why_wrong: B : Forme inexistante.
C : Réfléchi : ils partageraient avec eux-mêmes, pas l'un avec l'autre.
D : Pronom indéfini incomplet.

en.rule: Each other = reciprocity between two subjects.
why_wrong: B: Non-existent form.
C: Reflexive: they would share with themselves, not with one another.
D: Incomplete indefinite pronoun.
